
=== story.oldMillRoad ===
TRIAL 26 CRS 005000 · State of North Carolina v. Belinda Park
  Charges: Felony Death by Vehicle; Reckless Driving
  Defendant: Belinda Park, 29, Line cook; priors: 0; Released on a $75,000 secured bond; missed one court date early on, then was re-released.
  TEMPLATE story.oldMillRoad
  Summary: At about 11:52 p.m. on 26 December, Belinda Park's Honda Civic crossed the center line on a curve on Old Mill Road outside Bayard and struck a Toyota Corolla head-on. The Corolla's driver, Alex Fitzgerald, 34, a nurse driving home from a twelve-hour shift, died at the scene. Belinda Park, a line cook at Riverside Grill, had stayed after closing that night. A hospital blood test about ninety minutes after the crash and a second, State Crime Laboratory test about three hours after it disagree on whether Park was over the legal limit when the cars collided. Park says a deer came out of the tree line and she swerved.
  Verdicts: Felony Death by Vehicle: guilty; Reckless Driving: notGuilty
  [Count 1: Felony Death by Vehicle] Class D Felony, prior record level I | Presumptive range | Minimum 51, maximum 74 months. Active: committed to the custody of the N.C. Department of Adult Correction.
  [Commitment] Minimum term to be served before the defendant is eligible for release: 51 months (4 yr 3 mo). | Maximum term: 74 months. Earned time can move release toward the minimum, never below it; post-release supervision follows release. | Projected release: no earlier than 19 February 2031, and no later than 19 January 2032. | Upon release, the defendant will serve a period of post-release supervision (G.S. 15A-1368.2).
  [Monetary obligations] Court costs: US$213.00 | Restitution: US$13,000.00 | Appointed attorney fees: US$2,800.00 | Attorney appointment fee: US$60.00 | State Crime Laboratory fee: US$600.00 | Total: US$16,673.00
  [Victim notification] The District Attorney's victim-witness legal assistant will notify the victim of the judgment and of any release, appeal, or post-conviction hearing (N.C. Const. art. I, § 37).
  Reaction: District Attorney Alana Rasmussen: "We're grateful to the officers and witnesses who saw this case through."
  Reaction: Annette Burkhart: "We're disappointed, but the court listened. Park will do the time and come home."
  Reaction: Alex Fitzgerald's father, outside the courtroom: "It's not enough. It's never going to be enough."
  Reaction: Park's grandmother: "We'll be waiting when it's over."
  News: Guilty: Park case ends in conviction — A Hollis County judge has convicted Belinda Park on 1 of 2 counts of felony death by vehicle, and imposed 51 to 74 months in prison. At about 11:52 p.m. on 26 December, Belinda Park's Honda Civic crossed the center line on a curve on Old Mill Road outside Bayard and struck a Toyota Corolla head-on. Two groups gathered on opposite sides of the courthouse steps. District Attorney Alana Rasmussen: "We're grateful to the officers and witnesses who saw this case through." Park's grandmother: "We'll be waiting when it's over." Annette Burkhart: "We're disappointed, but the court listened. Park will do the time and come home." Park was taken into custody in the courtroom. The judgment includes US$16,673.00 in fines, fees, costs, and restitution.

=== story.churchBooks ===
TRIAL 26 CRS 005010 · State of North Carolina v. Antonia Beaumont
  Charges: Embezzlement ($100,000 or more)
  Defendant: Antonia Beaumont, 46, School bus mechanic; priors: 14; Held in the Hollis County jail on a $250,000 secured bond for 20 days.
  TEMPLATE story.churchBooks
  Summary: For six years Antonia Beaumont, a school bus mechanic for Hollis County Schools, served as the volunteer treasurer of Pleasant Grove Missionary Baptist Church in Cane Creek. When a new trustee asked for the building fund statements, $112,400 was gone, moved over three years in 41 checks and transfers to an account in the name of "DL Property Services." Beaumont says Pastor Earl Upchurch approved every payment as short-term loans to the contractor rebuilding the fellowship hall, and that the paperwork was handshakes. The pastor, now retired and in poor health, says no such arrangement existed.
  Verdicts: Embezzlement ($100,000 or more): guilty
  [Count 1: Embezzlement ($100,000 or more)] Class C Felony, prior record level V | Presumptive range | Minimum 101, maximum 134 months. Active: committed to the custody of the N.C. Department of Adult Correction.
  [Commitment] Minimum term to be served before the defendant is eligible for release: 101 months (8 yr 5 mo). | Maximum term: 134 months. Earned time can move release toward the minimum, never below it; post-release supervision follows release. | Credit for 20 days already served in pretrial confinement (G.S. 15-196.1). | Projected release: no earlier than 30 March 2035, and no later than 30 December 2036. | Upon release, the defendant will serve a period of post-release supervision (G.S. 15A-1368.2).
  [Monetary obligations] Court costs: US$213.00 | Total: US$213.00
  Reaction: ADA Candace Edgerton: "This is a fair result under the sentencing laws, and it's about public trust."
  Reaction: Anita Donnelly: "It's a hard day. We'll be talking with Beaumont about next steps."
  News: Beaumont headed to prison after embezzlement ($100,000 or more) conviction — Superior Court Judge Hale found Antonia Beaumont, 46, guilty, and imposed 101 to 134 months in prison, ending a case that began with an arrest in Cane Creek. According to court records, for six years Antonia Beaumont, a school bus mechanic for Hollis County Schools, served as the volunteer treasurer of Pleasant Grove Missionary Baptist Church in Cane Creek. Reaction outside the courthouse was split. ADA Candace Edgerton: "This is a fair result under the sentencing laws, and it's about public trust." Anita Donnelly: "It's a hard day. We'll be talking with Beaumont about next steps." Beaumont was taken into custody in the courtroom. Counting 20 days already served, the earliest possible release is 30 March 2035.

Coleridge's niece, who lives in Ohio, found the statements after she fell and was hospitalized. Dimitriou says Coleridge insisted on every gift and called Dimitriou "the only family who shows up." Coleridge, who has mild dementia but sometimes recalls things clearly, has told different people different things.

  Defendant: Adam Brower, 37, Registered nurse; priors: 0; Held without bond in the Hollis County jail for 54 days.
  TEMPLATE story.nightNurse
  Summary: Over seven weeks on the night shift of the cardiac step-down unit at Hollis Regional Medical Center, four patients who were not diabetic crashed with dangerously low blood sugar between 2 and 5 a.m. Three died: Joe Waddell, 71; Ernest Lyles, 64; and Mae Sellers, 80. Lab tests on stored blood showed high insulin with almost no C-peptide, a sign the insulin came from a needle, not the body. Adam Brower, a registered nurse, worked every one of those nights and had pulled insulin from the medication cabinet for patients who didn't need it. Brower says the cabinet log is unreliable, that other nurses used each other's badges, and that very sick elderly patients sometimes crash for no clear reason.

Nestor Willoughby, the pledge master who organized the gauntlet, is one of several brothers charged. Someone deleted footage from the cameras after the death; the police recovered it.

Earned time can move release toward the minimum, never below it; post-release supervision follows release. | Credit for 73 days already served in pretrial confinement (G.S. 15-196.1). | Projected release: no earlier than 7 March 2027, and no later than 7 May 2027. | Upon release, the defendant will serve a period of post-release supervision (G.S. 15A-1368.2).
